purpose: Test whether adding .depot/workflows to the default branch automatically registers a native Depot workflow and produces a native run for a matching push.
documentedRegistrationPath: The current Depot CI quickstart says to push and merge the .depot changes so automatic workflow triggers are registered, and says a push trigger on the default branch starts the first native run on merge. A direct push is not the documented merge step.

probe.sideEffects: none; both copies echo the commit SHA and upload no artifacts

depotWorkflowList.queryCommand: depot ci workflow list --repo Aquaticats/Monochromatic --name registration-probe --org l4zncjjbj5 --output json

result: The GitHub copy ran. No native Depot run was observed within about two minutes of the direct push. A direct push is not the documented merge step, so this probe does not establish that automatic registration is absent or broken; it only records a direct-push observation.
cleanup: The probe workflows and marker were removed in commit f8bc2d6c67; the workflow list was empty before cleanup.
nextPositiveControl: A PR merge of the same side-effect-free .depot workflow, or the documented migrate-and-merge flow, observed for a native run and a registered workflow.
limits: One direct-push observation, not a PR-merge observation.
A two-minute observation window; asynchronous registration after that window was not observed.
The probe is not a valid negative for the documented merge path; it does not prove registration is broken.
No claim that automatic registration is impossible.
